summary: Exact candidate 0ff2c1d35ce43c13eb822cf0a502dce5df535044 is a valid partial fix: it serializes eager communicator launches and excludes custom all-reduce from graph capture. It does not add bounded native failure, and the original two-rank CUDA/NVLink failure could not be executed on the single-GPU ROCm host.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before source contract: the recorded base has no SingleStreamGuard or graph-capture exclusion. This is not an original CUDA-deadlock reproduction.
Direct capture is rejected and both legacy and V2 selection paths decline custom all-reduce during capture.
Twelve focused eager ordering, launch-lock, capture-refusal, and adjacent capability tests passed.
A real HIP graph capture rejected the guard call and left guard state unchanged on gfx950.
Two host threads and two GPU streams produced ordered numeric result 2, matching CPU reference 2 on gfx950; no custom-all-reduce kernel ran.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 executed HIP capture-refusal and eager stream-ordering probes only. The original custom-all-reduce distributed kernel was not executed.
remaining_counterexamples: The JIT custom-all-reduce payload polling loop remains unbounded, so a rendezvous collision or a path that bypasses the Python guard still has no device-side timeout or recovery.
The legacy AOT custom-all-reduce barrier polling loops remain unbounded, so an eager host guard does not provide bounded failure after a protocol collision or bypass.
The original two-rank CUDA concurrent-stream case and concurrent replay of two CUDA graphs remain unverified on representative hardware.
remaining_limitations: The assigned host has one AMD gfx950 GPU with ROCm 7.2, not two NVIDIA A100 CUDA GPUs with NVLink and green contexts.
The original distributed CUDA deadlock, CUDA graph replay concurrency, CUDA compiler/ISA behavior, and device timeout behavior were not executable.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
No model weights or full serving workload were used.
